column1: # Obligation citations — goal 0009 (select which recorded context crosses a harness boundary).
# One row per discrete decision this increment makes, in the id space of the goal's own `Done when`
# clauses (docs/goals/0009-selective-context.md), each clause split where it holds several decisions:
#   D1      every selected record has an attributable disposition, and every written item pairs with the
#           ordinal it came from (the reconciliation of included + necessities + excluded with the read);
#   D2.1    the transformation's own classes, with counts, in the report; D2.2 the human report's lines
#           for them and the run's selection warning;
#   D3.1    a split pair carries its counterpart by default and the report discloses it; D3.2 the same
#           selection under --strict-selection is refused by name; D3.3 closure eligibility — a
#           counterpart the source's line leaves inactive refuses the whole selection (default as well
#           as strict), and never activates the record;
#   D4      the unflagged path is untouched — no row (see below);
#   D5.1    the specification's own space: an ordinal is a value the read supplied, never a position;
#           D5.2 an ill-formed specification is refused with the core's own sentence; D5.3 the CLI
#           answers the usage exit code and installs nothing;
#   D6.1    call↔result identity, ID-less included (the ambiguous shape is omitted, never inferred);
#           D6.2 operation lifecycle finality (a progress event is no call's outcome); D6.3 the same
#           event reaches the writer only from the record the read paired it with; D6.4
#           unknown-undischarged stays distinct from omitted-by-selection; D6.5 the calls and results a
#           compaction boundary accounts for; D6.6 retained-vs-carried ancestry; D6.7 the record's own
#           membership on the source's active line, taken before the cut;
#   D7.1    the other pairs are refused by name in the core (before a read); D7.2 the CLI refuses them
#           before the source is opened (the run's reader calls stay at zero);
#   X1      a document a selection already produced is refused as a selection input (the seam is not
#           guessed from a reduced stream);
#   X2      a selected window keeps the read's own recorded instants (nothing is re-timed by the cut).
# scripts/obligation-citations.py is the arbiter: every row's cited test must exist in the named package
# and run and pass, and the `citations` step is required — a tree that lost this file, or a citation that
# went stale, fails the gate instead of passing partially. Columns: rule_id, test, package, artifact.
# Tab-separated; `#` comments and blank lines are ignored; a rule id appears once.
# Deliberately not covered, with the reason (form-based: a row is one Go test in a package
# scripts/gate-targets.txt covers, so a rule whose gate evidence is a python case the required `selftest`
# step runs, or a native harness run, cannot hold one):
#   D4  — the default path is byte-identical to the pre-change tree. Its evidence is the throw-away
#         before/after probe (the goal's acceptance surface names this form): the probe converted the
#         committed file-backed fixtures — the new selection fixture included — through every route with no
#         selection flag in a pristine checkout of the base revision and in this tree, and the two outputs
#         — 55 conversions, 360 lines, digests over normalized bytes — are identical (`diff` exit 0). The
#         verbatim after-tree output is docs/evidence/0009-d4-probe.txt; the probe file itself was removed,
#         so no gate-runnable Go test stands behind the clause.
#   D7's and D3's native halves, and D6's negative cases at the wire level — the reference route's
#         native-load arm is scripts/codex-native-check.py's flagged pair of conversions, whose view
#         assertions the required `selftest` step runs as scripts/tests/test_codex_native_check.py's
#         test_the_selection_arms_own_checks_are_not_vacuous, and whose real loader run (Codex's own
#         app-server reading the converted bytes) is quoted in docs/evidence/0009-selective-context.md
#         §5 — a native harness run plus a python case, not a Go test. D6's negative cases are also
#         driven at the writer's own wire (the mutation table of §3), whose Go tests are the rows below.
#   The per-record fates of D1 reach the CLI as `--json`'s `selection.records` and the human block; the
#         rows hold that half in cmd/ccc, which is a gate package.
